How the compass is calculated

Economic right = 60% private economy + 40% free market. Authority = the average of security, autocracy and unitary scores. Traditionalism = 100 minus the progressive score. These are the original 12 Axes formulas.

The eight-region color map follows the original site. The graph is a summary; the complete 12-axis profile determines matches.

A CENTER THAT KEEPS THE DIFFERENCES

Why the median?

For four people, sort the scores on each axis and average the middle two. An unusually high or low value does not enter that midpoint.

For three people, use the middle score. For two, the median is their average and cannot suppress an outlier. One person simply retains their own scores.

No one is labeled or discarded as an outlier. The range, individual scores and median absolute deviation (MAD) stay visible.

4 people → sort → average the middle 2

A combined profile is synthetic. A high match to its median can still be a poor fit for one person. “Shared matches” makes that difference visible.

Sources, filters & calculation details

Source snapshot

The 48 scores are preserved exactly from the four supplied URLs. Matches were recomputed from the published data because the live API was unavailable. Original descriptions and questions are not reproduced.

Shared compatibility

For every candidate, take the lowest individual compatibility among the selected people. Rank that minimum highest first. Ties use the median individual score, then the mean, then the name. Each card shows all selected individual scores.

Median-profile mode scores the synthetic vector of selected axis medians. It is a different question. The minimum-score filter still requires every selected person to pass.

All 15 nonempty selections have been computed against the full source catalogs. The page retains the top 24 matches per category and method, eight field winners and 12 books. Search operates on those retained matches.

Original recommendation filters

Both match methods honor the original recommendation filter of every selected person. Osmar’s link specifies Catholic; the other links specify none. The source’s exclusion and exclusivity rules are retained. This describes a filter, not an inferred religious identity.

The compass is an illustrative projection. Matching uses the full 12-axis scoring formula: 42% per-axis similarity, 33% direction, 18% intensity, 7% worst-axis agreement. Matches are not probabilities or endorsements.
